title: Enterprise Identity Entitlements: Packaging experiments for contract-mandated auth and pricing flexibility
creator: Asha Raman
description: Run a set of pricing and packaging experiments to determine how contract-mandated identity controls (SAML SSO assertations + role-based entitlements) should map to product SKUs, pricing tiers, and enforceable contractual commitments. This ticket consolidates experiment design, stakeholder alignment, legal guardrails, and rollout criteria for enterprise deals that require explicit authZ guarantees in contract terms.
background: Sales and solutions teams have reported increasing demand from regulated customers for explicit contract language guaranteeing support for SAML-based SSO, attribute-mapped RBAC, and entitlements enforcement. Current contract templates are vague about 'supporting SSO' and do not tie guarantees to pricing/packaging. Legal has flagged risk if we promise more than our product can reliably deliver under Dedicated/Private deployments. We need to define: (1) which identity features are table-stakes vs. upsell, (2) objective SLAs/commitments for entitlements enforcement, and (3) a repeatable pricing addendum that can be operationalized.
experiment_hypothesis: If we surface a clear entitlement SKU that includes 'contract-grade SAML + mapped RBAC + audit logging' and price it as an incremental add-on, then deal velocity for regulated customers will increase while we limit open-ended contractual obligations and reduce bespoke legal negotiations by at least 30% over the next two quarters.
experiment_design:
We will run two parallel experiments over a 10-week window:
- Variant A (Baseline): Continue with current approach (SSO described in product doc, no explicit entitlement SKU).
- Variant B (Packaged Entitlement): Offer a clearly defined add-on SKU that includes: SAML integration support (IdP metadata + SCIM optional), RBAC role templates + attribute-mapping service, audit-log export to SIEM, and a documented upgrade path to Dedicated/Private deployments.
Sales will be randomized by account segment: enterprise prospects in regulated verticals (finance, health, public sector). Contracts for Variant B will include an addendum with limited commitments (e.g., response/triage SLAs for integration issues, support turnaround for role mapping, and a stated scope of enforceability).
Data collection: close rate, average negotiation cycles (days), legal redlines count, time-to-onboard SSO (days), and number of bespoke SSO/RBAC clauses requested.
metrics: Primary: deal close rate for targeted segment (baseline vs variant), % reduction in legal redlines requiring C-level approval. Secondary: time-to-onboard SSO integration, revenue uplift from entitlement SKU, # of support tickets related to entitlement scope.
success_criteria: 1) >= 15% relative lift in close rate for Variant B at statistically significant level OR 2) >= 30% reduction in legal redlines / bespoke contract cycles. AND operational readiness (ENG playbook + documented runbook for RBAC mapping) completed and validated in staging.
rollout_plan:
Week 0: finalize addendum language with Legal and Security; create entitlements SKU in pricing catalog.
Week 1-2: prepare sales enablement (playbook, objection handling doc, pricing calculator).
Week 3-12: run experiment with a subset of enterprise accounts, weekly sync with Sales and Legal.
Post-experiment: analyze results, iterate on SKU scope, and produce recommended contract language for wider rollout. If passing success criteria, target GA: contracts-2025.Q2.
risks_mitigation:
Risk: Product promises > engineering capability leading to escalations. Mitigation: scope entitlements narrowly (integration support windows, not guaranteed same-day fixes), add explicit out-of-scope list in addendum.
Risk: Sales attempts to upsell to customers without necessary infra (e.g., requiring Dedicated). Mitigation: include clear deployment prerequisites in SKU and tie billing to deployment type.
Risk: Legal unwilling to standardize addendum. Mitigation: provide tiered language (preferred/limited) and documented fallback process for exceptions.
decisions:
- Narrowed entitlement scope to 'integration support + RBAC mapping guidance + audit log export' rather than committing to 100% enforcement guarantee.
- Pricing to be positioned as a percentage uplift (15-25%) over base enterprise seat/license depending on number of IdP integrations.
- Require Dedicated or Private deployment for formal contractual guarantees; Hosted API customers can receive best-effort support but not the contractual SLA.
tradeoffs: We trade immediate higher perceived value (by promising end-to-end enforcement) for operational safety by keeping guarantees conditional on deployment type. This reduces short-term sales leverage but reduces legal/ops risk and makes commitments measurable.
open_questions: What minimum technical acceptance test (TAT) should be required before declaring an SSO/RBAC integration 'complete' in the contract?
How will we price multi-IdP customers (per-idp or per-tenant)?
Do we need an incident response SLA tied to entitlements or is a routing/triage SLA sufficient?
